segments.title: THE POSTBOX THAT ONLY HAS NOW
notes: Express Your Ideas To The World
The Present Moment Is All That Exists
segments.angle: How might I look at this problem from an entirely different perspective?

sources.text: Express Your Ideas To The World: Leaving your comment on something is like leaving a message in a particular time in space as a wanderer of the universe.
The Present Moment Is All That Exists: Forget the whole notion of the future. There is only today. If you want to do something, do it now.
Express Your Ideas To The World: Your ethereal thoughts that come lightly and infinitely can become real and concrete the moment you make a post or leave a comment.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Here's a note with a split down the middle. Half of it says leave your mark everywhere. The other half says there's only now. Which half do you want?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Leave the mark, of course. A message dropped into one particular moment is a stone set in a road, and the wanderers who come after will stumble on it and know that someone passed this way.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: A stone only lands in the present, Narrator. Your wanderer reads it on a Tuesday, not in your century. The message isn't sent to the past. It's sent now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the present is the stone and the road both, and every post is destiny laid down all at once. Its arrival was written the moment it was sent.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: It's a postbox, Narrator. On the corner, flap bent, slot worn pale. A letter goes in and sits in the dark until the van comes round. Nothing destined about it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ah, the humble postbox at the corner, its slot worn pale by countless hands. I find it sacred. Every letter inside is a small deed waiting for its destiny.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Sacred until the van empties it on Thursday. Let me try this on me, out loud: once I hit send, I stop holding the thought. That's the bit I like.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You are trying an idea on yourself in front of the audience, March, how bold of you. And I shall guess what you have hidden in the design of that very postbox. A crown in the slot, perhaps?

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Nothing hidden. Just a bit of slant on the flap. And a crown in a postbox would just get the post stuck.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You are close to a sermon, which I allow. But the sending was destined; every stamp was bought for it long before the letter was written.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Stamps get bought on a Tuesday, Narrator. Nobody has ever bought one for destiny.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You stand so close to the box that you cannot see the post you are standing in. Step back, March. Each message is a wanderer's message in time, and you have addressed yours to the wrong century.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: The wrong century? I sent mine the moment I hit enter, which is the only moment there is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the moment is the message, and you have proved my point while refusing to say so.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Fine, you're right. Anyway, the postbox is yours. Lunch is on the next card.

segments.title: WHY THE COMMENT ARRIVES LATE
notes: Express Your Ideas To The World
The Present Moment Is All That Exists
segments.angle: If I knew absolutely nothing about this topic or context, what questions would I ask? What would seem confusing or counter-intuitive?

sources.text: Express Your Ideas To The World: Leaving your comment on something is like leaving a message in a particular time in space as a wanderer of the universe.
The Present Moment Is All That Exists: The past is behind us and when the future comes, it comes as the present.
Create And Die Empty: Die empty. Get every idea out of your head and into reality.
The Present Moment Is All That Exists: The past is history, and the future's a mystery.
Express Your Ideas To The World: Don't be afraid to speak your mind.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Okay, I know nothing. Why does a comment count if nobody reads it today?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Because the wanderer reads it when he arrives. Patience is the traveller's gift.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Arrives where? It's sitting there now, Narrator.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Yes, and it is already on its way, like a ship seen far off on the sea.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: That's a lot of sea for one comment. What's a wanderer?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Anyone who passes through, March. You, me, and whoever stumbles on us.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: So every reader is a wanderer. Great, now I'm a traveller.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Better. I offer J a new title: Keeper of the Unsent Letters.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Titles are cheap, Narrator. And the kettle clicked because it boils.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your kettle clicked the moment I named him. Destiny has a sense of timing.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Creating matters, so why die empty? Why not save something?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Because the future is a mystery, and empty hands are the only honest ones.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Honest hands still need a cup of tea, Narrator.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Keep the tea. Empty the rest.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Last one: people hide in the crowd anyway. Why does anyone need telling?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They do, March. Most keep their voice in a purse like a coin.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: I'm keeping score, and you're still one behind. Not telling you what I hid.

segments.title: A SMALL TEST OF DOING IT NOW
notes: Express Your Ideas To The World
The Present Moment Is All That Exists
segments.angle: What data or evidence currently supports this idea? What data would disprove it or force a major revision? How could I test this with a small experiment?

sources.text: The Present Moment Is All That Exists: "If you want to do something, do it now." Derek Sivers wrote that people think they'll do something later, when there is only today.
The Present Moment Is All That Exists: "A second passed is a second lost. Treasure every single second so that there is no regret."
Express Your Ideas To The World: "Leaving your comment on something is like leaving a message in a particular time in space as a wanderer of the universe."

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Okay, I'll test it on me. If only now exists, I should be able to act now.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dear girl, the present is a river, and you have only to step into its current. The banks take care of themselves.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: That's not a test. Give me something I can count.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Count? The present is not for counting, March. It is for living. Quite simple, really.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Don't call it simple. I hate that word.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Forgive me. The test is humble, but the living is grand.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Fine. I post a comment, then count who reads it an hour later. Nobody reads it, the idea's wrong.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then you have lost before you began, because the wanderer arrives in his own time, not yours.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: That's unfalsifiable. Lovely for you, useless for me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then let me take the chair while you think, March. A storyteller ought to sit where the story is told.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Sit back down. Evidence first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What would disprove it, then? A clock that stops?

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: A comment nobody can ever see. Then I'd revise the whole idea.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ah, I see it now. You have hidden something in your design, a little gift folded under the words.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: You're guessing. And that's another one for me. Keep up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Perhaps a small experiment in a drawer, waiting for its hour.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Guess again tomorrow, Narrator.

segments.title: THE FAILURE THAT FERTILISES THE HEAP
notes: Express Your Ideas To The World
The Present Moment Is All That Exists
segments.angle: Imagine this idea has been implemented and failed spectacularly one year from now. What are the most likely reasons for its failure? How could we mitigate those risks now?

sources.text: The Present Moment Is All That Exists: Forget the whole notion of the future. There is only today. If you want to do something, do it now.
Create And Die Empty: It's better to create something bad than nothing at all. You can improve something bad. You can't improve nothing.
Create And Die Empty: Most of what you make will be fertiliser for the few that turn out great. But you won't know which is which until afterward.
The Present Moment Is All That Exists: A second passed is a second lost. Treasure every single second so that there is no regret.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Okay, the angle. It's a year from now and the idea's a crater. You act now with no planning, the post goes up, and nobody's there. That's the failure.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A crater is a fine place to stand, March. The failed post is the ground the next one grows from. You can improve something bad, and you can improve a crater too.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Ground is not a plan. Acting now without a plan is just noise with a timestamp.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Noise is what most of us make before the few great pieces appear. Fertiliser, March. You will not know which heap was the soil until the harvest is over.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Lovely. So the mitigation is to have a heap. That's just hoping with compost.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: No, the mitigation is to act now and keep the list short. Forget the clutter of the future and the risks shrink to what is in front of you.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: What's in front of me is a comment box. What can go wrong with a comment box?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Everything, which is why each second matters. A second lost in fear is the real failure, and nobody reads that in a year.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Fine. Mitigation one: check the wording, the link, and the time it goes live. Those are things I can see now, not future things.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sensible. You are, I suspect, building a fortress with a comment box at its gate.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Fine, you're right. Moving on. What kills the idea fastest?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nothing kills it fastest, March. Nothing is the one failure you cannot improve.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Ouch. Write the risk list now, before this kettle boils.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ah, the kettle. It clicked the moment you said it, which is destiny keeping time for the both of us.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Destiny doesn't pay the electric bill. Tomorrow you tell me what's folded under my design.

segments.title: THE FEAR UNDER THE POSTBOX
notes: Express Your Ideas To The World
The Present Moment Is All That Exists
segments.angle: What is the fundamental problem or need that this note/idea is trying to address? Is it addressing a symptom or the root cause? (Think: Five Whys)

sources.text: Express Your Ideas To The World: “If we hide or hinder ourselves in fear of rejection of others, are we not in essence, rejecting ourselves first?” _- Robert Pantano_
Express Your Ideas To The World: Leaving your comment on something is like leaving a message in a particular time in space as a wanderer of the universe.
Create And Die Empty: Most of what you make will be fertiliser for the few that turn out great.
The Present Moment Is All That Exists: A second passed is a second lost. Treasure every single second so that there is no regret.
The Present Moment Is All That Exists: The past is history, and the future's a mystery.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Okay, strip off the timing, the planning, and the heap. What's left is fear of being turned down. Pantano says it outright: the hiding is the rejecting.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ah, the wound beneath the wound. Every grand work begins in a flinch, and the flinch is merely the first draft of the self.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Keep it plain. A comment is a message that never leaves the desk. The root is the bottle never getting sent, not the clock.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wanderer only finds a message that was posted, March. You have been a wanderer yourself, pausing at other people's words and moving on.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: I'm a wanderer who counts readers an hour later and still doesn't know the number. That's my test, not my wound.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then hear the hard truth, which I will not sweeten. Most of what you make will be fertiliser for the few that turn out great.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Fine, but fertiliser is the symptom again. Ask why you're scared to make the heap at all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Because the heap looks like a verdict. Every pile reads as proof you were never the great one. That fear is real, and it will outlast this note.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Good, that's the root. The waiting, the kettle, the risk lists, they're all branches off one fear of being unwanted.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Branches, yes, but a branch cannot grow without its tree, which is the self refusing itself. Pantano wrote that before either of us had a desk.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Which is why the time line lands. A second lost is only lost if you were scared to spend it. Treasure every second so there's no regret.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Regret is the cheapest prayer there is. But I concede the clock: it is merely the fear with a dial on it.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: That's one point to me on the root, and the score stays in my head where you can't see it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Cheating, and I suspect you have kept that score since the kettle first clicked. Very well. For the run I give J a title: Wayfarer of the Open Postbox.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: No. He doesn't get a crown for a comment. Also, the whole drawer of your titles is stationery, and none of it gets mailed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The past is history, and the future's a mystery, as the note says. You hide your design in a drawer, and I hand out crowns, and we both wait for the present to walk up to the box.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Verdict: the root is fear, the symptom is the waiting, and I was right about the root. You were right about the heap. Tomorrow's comment still goes up. Up next: Habits Become Automatic - Your New Identity, then How Our Brains Interpret Imagined And Real Experiences.

segments.title: THE SHOES LEFT BY THE DOOR
notes: Habits Become Automatic - Your New Identity
How Our Brains Interpret Imagined And Real Experiences
segments.angle: Cross Pollination: Find the intersection of key ideas between two or more notes.

sources.text: Habits Become Automatic - Your New Identity: Old habits are who you are. New habits, should they stick, will eventually become old habits.
How Our Brains Interpret Imagined And Real Experiences: The brain learns from repetition. If you hear something enough times, your brain will start to believe it's true.
How Our Brains Interpret Imagined And Real Experiences: Vividly imagining a situation is literally the same as experiencing it, as far as your brain's concerned.
How Our Brains Interpret Imagined And Real Experiences: Mental practice is as powerful as actual practice.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Okay, the note says old habits are who you are. So the shoes by the door are the person, not the jog.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ah, the shoes are a vow, waiting in the hall with the patience of a sentry. Every great run begins with footwear that refuses to leave the house without you.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: They're runners, not vows. You leave them out because starting tomorrow is easier when you trip over them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the stumble is the sermon. You tread on the habit each morning until the habit treads back upon you.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: The brain learns from repetition, and tripping is repetition. That's the note, not your sermon.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Imagining the run is running, as the note says, so the shoes are already laced. I have worn them in my mind for years, through every mountain pass I never climbed.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Mental practice is as powerful as actual practice, the note says. But you still haven't gone out the door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: I concede the door. Still, the boots and the drawer and my chair are all one sentence about waiting, and I have been reading it aloud for an hour.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Stay out of my chair. You want it because I keep my score there and you can't read it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: I can read the score perfectly. I merely decline to admit how far ahead you are, the way one keeps a cushion warm for a guest who never arrives.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: You were right.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Now, what's under my design? Guess again, and this time make it sensible.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The drawer holds a crown no one will mail. Or a map. Or a single shoe, which would be fitting for a man who only waits.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Wrong, every time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then I shall make my move on the chair, where destiny keeps the score and the kettle keeps its clock.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Keep the chair warm. I've got a comeback saved for when you're comfortable.

segments.title: THE PATH THAT WALKS YOU
notes: Habits Become Automatic - Your New Identity
How Our Brains Interpret Imagined And Real Experiences
segments.angle: Create a simple analogy or metaphor to explain the core concept of this note. What does this analogy reveal about its strengths or weaknesses?

sources.text: Habits Become Automatic - Your New Identity: Old habits are who you are.
How Our Brains Interpret Imagined And Real Experiences: Your nervous system cannot tell the difference between an imagined experience and a real one.
How Our Brains Interpret Imagined And Real Experiences: Think and speak only the grandest narrative for yourself.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Try it on me. I'm a runner who answers comments late. The note says each late answer is a vote. So who do I become?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You become a slow tide, March, a woman who answers each message only when the moon permits, and every late reply is a stone dropped into a well that answers back in the voice of your grandmother.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: That's a poster. Give me something I can walk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Very well. Imagine a path worn through long grass, where the walker is not one soul but every soul who ever crossed the meadow, pressing the stalks flat until the crossing is simply the road.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Good. Walk it daily, the grass stays flat. Stop, it grows back. The weak bit: a path goes wherever feet went, even off a cliff.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the cliff is merely the path's honest ambition, and the walker who strides over the edge has at least kept faith with the grass.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Stop being poetic at a cliff. Short version: I walk the path, I'm a walker. Done.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tomorrow your walker will be shorter by a single stride, and the stride will be missed by no one but the grass.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Brain bit, quick.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The nervous system cannot tell the difference between an imagined experience and a real one. So you may imagine the cliff so faithfully that you fall off it in your sleep, rejoicing.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: That's yours, sure. Mirrors next.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A mirror, yes. It shows you the face you wear this minute, so you are whatever it reflects, which is splendid for a vain man and grave for a woman with a deadline.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Mirror's worse. It shows the now and nothing of the walk. You can't see your legs in it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You keep winning the instruments, which is unfair, as I had only just polished the glass. Still, the mirror was mine first and you have scratched it.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: Think and speak only the grandest narrative. So say mine aloud, in your voice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Stand straighter. Speak to the room as though the room has paid for the tickets. Say: I am the walker, bold of stride, and the grass bows as I pass.

lines.speaker: march
lines.text: I am the walker, bold of stride. There. Feels like a costume I haven't tried on yet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then I stay in the chair, guess again what sits under your design, and let the cliff keep its appointment.
